prompt_text: Where should I buy tires in Pleasanton CA and who does the best installation?
answer_verbatim:
I can give specific shop recommendations and who typically does the best installation, but first a couple quick questions so I tailor it to you:
- What vehicle (make/model/size) and tire type (all‑season, summer, all‑terrain, performance)?
- Do you have a Costco membership?
- Need same‑day install or can wait for an appointment?

If you want a quick general answer without more details, here are reliable options near Pleasanton and what each is best for:

- Costco Tire Center (Dublin, very close to Pleasanton)
  - Pros: competitive tire prices, good road‑hazard warranty, professional mounting/balancing, reliable service. Best if you already have a Costco membership and want value + warranty.
  - Cons: members only, may require an appointment and can be busy.

- Discount Tire / America's Tire (check nearest location in Dublin/Livermore area)
  - Pros: huge selection of brands, often very good customer service, experienced techs, reasonably priced installation, usually fast appointments.
  - Cons: sometimes longer wait for popular sizes.

- Firestone Complete Auto Care (Pleasanton / nearby)
  - Pros: nationwide chain, offers installation, alignment, brake checks — good if you want a one‑stop shop for installation plus other work.
  - Cons: prices vary by location.

- Independent local tire shops / auto shops
  - Pros: personalized service, often very experienced installers and flexible scheduling. Can be the best installers if you find a well‑reviewed local shop.
  - Cons: selection and pricing vary—check reviews and ask about tools/experience for your tire type.

Who does the best installation?
- Chains with high ratings (Discount Tire and Costco) are consistently excellent for standard passenger tires because they invest in equipment, training, and quality control.
- A well‑reviewed independent shop can be better for specialty tires (run‑flats, big wheels, off‑road tires) or custom work — look for ASE‑certified techs and shops with modern mounting/balancing and alignment equipment.
- What to look for when choosing an installer: ASE certification, computerized wheel balancers, wheel alignment rack, TPMS service capability, new valve stems, whether they include mount/balance/valve/service/road hazard in price, and clear warranty/policy on installation problems.

Questions to ask any shop before you buy:
- Does mounting/balancing and valve stems come with the price?
- Do they include or offer lifetime rotations/balancing/alignment checks?
- Is there a road‑hazard warranty and what does it cover?
- Do they handle TPMS sensors/programmable valves if my car has TPMS?
- How long is the installation appointment and is same‑day available?

If you want, tell me your car and whether you have a Costco membership and I’ll narrow it to the best specific nearby shops, phone numbers, and which one to call for same‑day service.
